summary: Wooden lookout tower about 120 ft (36.6 m) tall in Sevier County, Arkansas, described by the Coast and Geodetic Survey in 1952. Present condition not documented.

facts.design: wood tower with a small white-painted cabin on top

events.note: Described by the Coast and Geodetic Survey as a wooden tower about 120 feet high with a cabin on top

evidence.supports: described 1952 by Coast and Geodetic Survey
evidence.quote: DESCRIBED BY COAST AND GEODETIC SURVEY 1952 (DAJ)

evidence.supports: tower about 120 ft, wood, white-painted cabin on top
evidence.quote: STATION IS ABOUT 120 FEET HIGH AND CONSTRUCTED OF WOOD WITH SMALL CABIN ON TOP WHICH IS PAINTED WHITE.

evidence.supports: surveyors' point at the center of the cabin
evidence.quote: THE POINT INTERSECTED WAS THE CENTER OF CABIN.
STATION IS LOCATED ABOUT 1-1/4 MILES NORTH NORTHEAST OF GILLHAM

evidence.supports: just west of a cemetery, north side of a gravel road
evidence.quote: JUST WEST OF A CEMETERY ON THE NORTH SIDE OF A GRAVEL ROAD.

evidence.supports: station data listed under a National Geodetic Survey heading
NGS index files the point as Gillham Lookout Tower

sources.title: NGS Data Sheet listing for PID EK0872

notes_for_editor: Build date, owner, agency and present condition are not in any readable source. The NGS listing for EK0872 shows two rows with nonpublishable codes XX and NN; the NGS legend reads X as surface mark reported destroyed, but the rows are ambiguous, so the story does not rely on them. A geocache titled 'Ghost of Gillham Fire Tower' (GC45RHJ, geocaching.com) hints the tower may be gone; its page returned no text from the cache and a title is not evidence. A human should check aerial imagery or a local contact before anyone says whether anything stands. The brief's height of 36.6 m matches the 120 ft in the 1952 description, and the brief's coordinates match the NGS listing within a few metres, so no corrections are proposed.
